title: Choose the quiet direction
question: No pitch, no theme, no oversized slogan. Which structure feels most naturally like you?

options.label: Quiet Record
options.lineage: personal records, plain chronology, and restrained editorial systems
options.thesis: A short introduction and a factual record do the work without announcing a brand concept.
options.viewport: A fixed, human introduction sits beside one continuous chronology of current roles and selected work.
options.risk: It relies on strong writing and spacing; weak copy has nowhere to hide.

options.label: Margin Notes
options.lineage: working notebooks, marginalia, and quiet technical writing
options.thesis: The main column speaks plainly while dates, tools, and context live as small notes at the edge.
options.viewport: One readable column carries the biography; a narrow margin indexes roles and projects without cards.
options.risk: The notebook character can feel overly literary if annotations become decorative.

options.label: Work Index
options.lineage: studio indexes, changelogs, and well-kept project directories
options.thesis: A compact index lets the work lead, with personal context revealed in the same measured system.
options.viewport: A modest biography leads directly into a dense list of projects, roles, dates, and links.
options.risk: It may feel too impersonal if the opening paragraph is shortened further.

canonCard.label: Contemporary developer portfolio
canonCard.thesis: Direct biography, sticky context, an experience list, and quiet interaction at the craft level of strong current personal sites.
canonCard.viewport: A left introduction remains visible while experience and work scroll on the right.
canonCard.risk: Highly usable, but familiar enough to resemble many developer portfolios.
